newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition improves with warm weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition improves with warm weather.

text.p: Unseasonably warm weather allowed the Texas wheat crop to improve during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
"Warm, windy weather conditions dominated the weather in all areas during the week. Growing conditions for small grains and winter pastures were very good," the report said.
The report said the rapid changes in the weather from the previous week caused some stress on cattle, but the need for supplemental feeding slowed.
Good cotton harvest progress occurred in the Plains, and yields continued to be good in most fields.
Texas wheat was rated 80 percent of normal, versus 76 percent last week and 50 percent last year.
Sorghum harvested 100 percent vs 99 w/a, 100 y/a, 100 avg.
Cotton harvested 90 percent vs 82 w/a, 91 y/a, 88 avg.
Pasture and range condition was rated 31 percent good to excellent, versus 38 percent at that level last week.
